Wallet, round three: on a phone a bar stays on top with Account, Send, Rules and Activity, and shows a number when something waits for you. Ask to be paid gets a Share button on phones. Your address book can go along between the simulation and Live node; each address keeps its check words, and the simulation's made-up accounts stay behind. With a full inbox your own last two payments stay in view. Clicking into a rule's value ticks its block. When the real testnet has nothing to vote on, one button takes you to the Telegram alerts. Testnet only, test AGRS have no value.

Wallet: fair turns on the testnet’s two rule places. Tau Testnet Alpha lets only two accounts hold a personal rule at a time, and whoever holds one keeps it until they remove it. Now, when you sign a rule in the wallet, it also signs the rule’s removal for later and leaves it with our relay. Your turn lasts a day while nobody waits; once someone joins the line, it ends 30 minutes after you took the place, and the relay sends the removal for you, even if your tab is closed. When both places are taken you can join the line, see your place in it, and the page tells you when a place is free.

Build pulse, a new page under Explore: how Tau's code is moving, read from the public git history of IDNI's tau-testnet and tau-lang repositories. The newest changes with the parts of the code they touched, a year of weekly rhythm, which areas moved in the last 4 and 12 weeks, tags, and which commit our testnet node is built from compared with the newest one. A timeline lays commits beside the testnet's restarts. Commits come in batches, so the page shows what moves, not who is fast. Unofficial, refreshed every 30 minutes; Developers links to it and to its JSON.

major.title: New: Build pulse, how Tau's code is moving
major.text: The newest changes in IDNI's public tau-testnet and tau-lang code, which parts move, a year of weekly rhythm and the version the testnet node runs. Read from public git history, unofficial.

html: Alerts read patterns, not just events: the same rule change on repeat is now one line (“3× …”) or no second post at all, and practice votes are explained instead of listed, for example “all from one account, which looks like someone testing the vote flow”. When the same proposal comes again and again within an hour, the channel gets one finding that says what it most likely means.

Findings: our first code fix is now with IDNI. When their bootnode refused new peers for three hours on 29 October, nodes that had lost it stayed stuck even after it came back. We sent IDNI a pull request with tests that makes a node with no peers dial its bootstrap peers again every minute; its status shows live on the page.

In numbers can now switch to Agorzilla, our second site at agorzilla.com: its visitors, counted the same cookie-free way and kept apart from Tau HUD's own numbers. The privacy notice covers agorzilla.com too.

Findings: a second fix is with IDNI. Two tests of time-based rules that were switched off in IDNI's checks pass on real Tau, so we asked to switch them back on. The page also lists our two newest requests, a free place for personal rules and a live consensus switch. With more findings than fit, each card shows its title and status and keeps the short summary for the hover.

Alerts: Agorzilla's evening now comes to the Telegram channel. When its daily choice closes at 18:00 UTC, one short post says what changed, how many days it has lived and what is open tonight. Telegram only, test AGRS only.

HUD: a small Agorzilla breathes in the empty middle of the top line, wherever the header has room for it. Click to visit agorzilla.com, the creature the community feeds with real testnet transactions; its hover shows how often it was fed today and its stage, once agorzilla.com shares those numbers.

HUD: Agorzilla in the header is bigger and stands exactly in the middle between the notice and the status chips, as tall as both header lines, with a soft shadow under his feet. Where something on the second line would be under him, he steps aside.

HUD: Agorzilla now stands on the header's bottom line, right next to the live status he keeps an eye on, and a little taller. He never covers a button: where the header is too tight for him, on smaller screens and phones, he stays away.

Wallet, ready for everyone: on Live node, while both of the testnet’s rule places are taken, the Rules panel now says so in one line with both ways out, Continue in the simulation or Join the line, and everything fits on one screen again. A sign button that cannot sign yet is now an outline instead of a dim green. Your place in the line shows the moment you make your account. Tabbing through the rule fields no longer ticks them. Testnet only, test AGRS have no value.

major.title: Wallet: a day of fixes, ready to try
major.text: The Tau HUD testnet wallet after a day of rounds with simulated users: check words on every address, a way back for first payments, a pay-me link with QR code, fair turns on the two live rule places, and clear reasons wherever a button is grey. Keys stay in your browser. Testnet only, test AGRS have no value.

html: HUD: tauhud.com/?view=core shows only the Chain core of the live chain, filling the frame, with the block height underneath, for other sites to show in a frame. The hovers work as on the HUD, and a click opens Tau HUD. Agorzilla's site uses it to show that its falling blocks and the HUD follow the same chain.
Agorzilla gets its own voice on X: every evening's result and each new growth stage are posted on Agorzilla's own X account, with the creature on a dark card and without links, at most a few a day.

HUD: Agorzilla now stands on the header line right next to the Live status on every screen. On screens where the page is centred or scaled he used to land too far right with his feet below the line. He also follows the status chips the moment they change width. The core-only view for other sites gains bg=none (transparent) and quiet=1 (no labels or hovers), and tells the page around it when it is ready and when each block lands.

HUD: Agorzilla now sits a touch lower, so his feet rest on the header line instead of hovering just above it. On screens around 2000 px wide he also stays beside the Live status instead of slipping further right.
Every post on X from @TauHUDcom now ends with #TauNet and $AGRS, once, after the line that says where it comes from. No other tags are added, and the caps and the no-repeat rules stay.

Node: our node now runs IDNI's newest testnet software (b1ebfa4). It carries IDNI's two fixes from the evening of 29 October: the p2p overflow that stopped the bootnode from accepting peers for three hours, and a restart for a node whose network has died. Findings shows both next to our own reconnect fix.

New: Agorzilla, our second site at agorzilla.com. One creature that everyone shares on Tau Testnet Alpha: each meal is a real testnet transaction from a test wallet the page makes in your browser, and every evening at 18:00 UTC the change most wallets picked becomes part of it. Test AGRS have no value; feeding buys nothing. The small Agorzilla in the HUD header leads there too.

major.title: New: Agorzilla, one creature the whole testnet feeds and shapes
major.text: Each meal is a real transaction on Tau Testnet Alpha, sent from a test wallet the page makes in your browser. Every evening at 18:00 UTC the change most wallets picked becomes part of it. Test AGRS have no value.

html: Donations, worded plainly: the About section and the Updates card are now called Donations and say that a donation is a voluntary gift that buys nothing, with no promise about the future of the site. The thank-you posts and the privacy notice say the same.

Tau HUD in numbers: a new “Testnet transactions” split shows how much of the testnet's traffic comes from Agorzilla (meals and votes), from Tau HUD pages (wallet, playground, vote) and from elsewhere, counted by wallet, not by person. Below it, how many pages were opened from a link on the other site.

Follow along, easier to find: every page's footer ends with Follow and the marks for Telegram, X and Agorzilla on X. The Get alerts menu and About also link Agorzilla on X, and About has a button for each channel.

Agorzilla on the HUD is alive: he breathes, blinks, looks around and at the Live status, scratches, stretches, yawns in the evening and walks a little to the left where the header has room, never further right than his spot. He also reacts to the network: an ear twitch for a block, a cheer for an agreed rule, a head shake for a refused transfer, a squint when ghosts pile up and worry when no block comes. Never more than one move every 8 seconds; with reduced motion he only blinks.

Agorzilla on the HUD now really walks: his legs step in turn, front left with back right, while his body rides up on each step, and his paws stand in front of the header line. Now and then he does a special move, sized to the room on your screen: a little dance, a backflip where there is head room, a roll or a cartwheel along the line where there is space to his left. Agorzilla also has its own entry in the Playground menu.

Accounts: every validator has its own profile now. Open a validator’s account and it shows the blocks it made over time and its share of all blocks, the pauses between its blocks, the hours of the last 7 days in which it made one, every validator side by side, what it sent by kind, the fees it paid, and how it voted on rule changes. The Account button shows its balance and rules as before.

major.title: Validator profiles: who makes the blocks, and how reliably
major.text: Open any validator on Tau HUD and see the blocks it made over time, its share of all blocks, the pauses between them, the hours it was up in the last 7 days, and how it voted on rule changes. Live from our node, or in the simulation with six validators. Testnet only, test AGRS have no value.

html: Click a validator in the Chain core and its profile opens: what it sealed, how much traffic it carried and how it voted (the Validators panel's detail has the same link). The header Agorzilla's hover now reads like a Chain core element: a status light, Live with today's meals and wallets, his stage and tonight's vote, all from agorzilla.com. His eyes now look where he looks, and skin lids with a lash line close when he blinks.

Japanese version: the whole site now reads in 日本語; switch with the EN | 中文 | 日本語 pill in the header or open any page with ?lang=ja. Every HUD hover, the guided tours, the newspaper as its own Japanese edition, the press kit and the story at tauhud.com/story/ja are translated, and the choice is remembered. Colours stay as in English, green for good news.

major.title: New: Tau HUD in Japanese
major.text: The whole site now reads in 日本語: every page, every HUD hover, the guided tours, the newspaper and the story. Switch with EN | 中文 | 日本語 in the header.

html: The header Agorzilla's mouth opens for real now: dark inside with a pink tongue when he yawns, a little open on a cheer when a vote passes, and now and then his tongue peeks out on its own. Also fixed: the rule change card under the Chain core no longer says “NaN blocks” when the proposal's height is unknown.
